title: Why Do We Laugh? The Evolutionary Puzzle of Humor
question: What is laughter actually for, and why does an involuntary, energy-costly reflex get triggered by something as abstract as a joke?
summary: Laughter is loud, involuntary, and evolutionarily expensive, yet universal across human cultures and present in tickled apes. Competing theories from biology, neuroscience, and social psychology each explain part of why we do it—but not all of it.
